adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents()` now iterates each destination and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` (packages/core/EventManager.ts around the new `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop). However, only Google’s service actually selects the calendar based on the credential (`GoogleCalendarService.createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)` uses `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` to pick `calendarId`). In contrast, Lark and Office365 mechanically destructure the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`) and CalDAV/BaseCalendarService filters by only the first destination calendar externalId as well. This means when creating events for secondary hosts in collective/team scenarios, those non-Google services will still target the first destination’s `externalId` regardless of which host credential is being used, potentially creating the event on the wrong calendar or failing. Meanwhile `CalendarManager.createEvent` returns `externalId` from the loop input (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts adds `externalId` to the result), so persisted references can point to a calendar where the event was not actually created.
